rows.name: spoken-why-warps-frozen-5
rows.question: Why?
rows.answer: Because a GPU shares instruction-execution hardware across the 32 threads in a warp, it is most efficient when they execute the same instructions on different data. When threads take different branches, the GPU executes the required paths with only the relevant threads active, reducing useful parallel work. Accessing consecutive memory locations also helps because the GPU can combine those accesses into fewer memory transactions.

rows.question: Why?
rows.answer: Interpreting “y” as “why”: “unreliable” describes a customer experience, not a single root cause, so we need to distinguish missed deliveries, wrong refills, and misleading updates before choosing a fix. Tracing affected orders shows where the service actually breaks down rather than where we suspect it does. Prioritizing safety and essential-supply risks first, then the largest recurring failure, directs effort toward the greatest customer harm.
